Going down, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,6); going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
I can't rule out left or up yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.

Going down would leave both cell (6,1) and number 3 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going to number 2, the next 8 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,6). So the line goes up.
Going right, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,4). So the line goes left.
Going up would strand number 2: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going up would force the line onto number 6 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Cell (4,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going up, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 6. So the line goes right.
Going right would force the line onto number 6 before its turn. So the line goes up.
Going up would cut off the top-right corner (6 cells); going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Cell (3,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Cell (2,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going left would leave both cell (1,1) and cell (3,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
